correctness.rationale: For z in B_c0(X), choose three distinct coordinates with norm<=1/3. For a Delta-point d in X set q_j=(3z_mj-d)/2; exact triangle inequality gives norm<=1. Form u^(r) with d in one chosen coordinate, q_j in other chosen coordinates and z elsewhere. Finite modifications preserve c0(X); each u^(r) has a Delta-point coordinate, hence is a Delta-point by the published coordinate-lifting lemma. At each chosen coordinate (d+2q_j)/3=z_mj, while all other coordinates are unchanged. Boundary norms and z=0 are covered. This is a full algebraic proof, not a computational extrapolation.
